transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Hi doctor. I've been feeling extremely restless lately, constantly "on the go" as if I'm driven by a motor. It's gotten to the point where I have a really hard time staying seated when I'm supposed to, like during work meetings or dinners.
Have you struggled with this restlessness and difficulty staying still for most of your life since childhood, or does it come and go in distinct periods?

Yes, I've actually struggled with this since childhood, definitely starting before I was 12, and it doesn't really come and go in episodes. It has been a constant, everyday issue for about a year and two months now.
Along with the restlessness, do you often find it hard to focus, keep track of things, or finish tasks because you get easily distracted?
To be honest, I don't really have much trouble focusing or getting easily distracted. My main struggle is just this constant physical urge to move and not being able to sit still.
Do you often experience excessive, hard-to-control worry or anxiety about everyday things like your work, health, or daily chores?
No, I don't really experience excessive or hard-to-control worry about everyday things like that. I might get a bit frustrated when I can't sit still, but I wouldn't say I struggle with anxiety.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Based on the patient's explicit denial of excessive, hard-to-control worry about everyday things, Generalized Anxiety Disorder is ruled out. The patient's presentation of lifelong (onset before age 12) hyperactivity and restlessness without significant inattention confirms the diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation).
